findings.title: Production Full Short durable observer never acknowledges the new capture-complete transition
findings.trigger: Complete valid SSE message_stop with either clean EOF or a later ReadTimeout, using current FullShortDispatchLedgerObserverV1 as attempt_observer.
findings.observed: The real observer writes exact bytes, creates the independent anchor, and records a receipt, then implicitly returns None. The new adapter requires capture_ack is True. In both independently executed cases the receipt audit is authoritative and observer.provider_protocol_capture_complete() is True, while owner.terminal_capture_complete is False and its trace has no CAPTURE_COMMITTED.
findings.expected: A completed and independently anchored production capture must acknowledge the same capture state used by the shared stream owner. The contract explicitly names this Full Short observer as a durable boundary.
findings.impact: The advertised shared completeness representation is false on the actual durable production observer. Synthetic observers that explicitly return True do not establish this production integration. This is a current source behavior, not a rejection because a future Full Short has not run.
findings.reproduction: reviews/reviewer-2-repro-result.json: clean and timeout cases, reproduced_missing_durable_ack=true; persisted_capture_authoritatively_audited=true
findings.required_boundary: Wire the real durable observer acknowledgment to the owner and verify both complete-success tail and Provider-error cases through the production durable observer. No automatic fix performed.

findings.title: Full Short loses the distinct unclean transport-tail observation at durable projection
findings.trigger: Same complete successful response followed by ReadTimeout through the real Full Short observer.
findings.observed: The owner correctly observes transport_tail_closed_cleanly=False and tail_counts.TIMEOUT=1, but the persisted capture metadata and attempt keep only transport_complete=True. _model_response_from_body omits body._shared_stream_state, and the Full Short attempt contains no tail/outcome fields. The clean EOF and timeout cases therefore have the same persisted completeness semantics even though their owner outcomes differ.
findings.expected: Keep terminal success and durable capture accepted while retaining the separately typed unclean transport tail at the actual execution evidence boundary, as the probe campaign already does with stream_outcome_v1.
findings.impact: Restart or post-run evidence review cannot recover whether this production response ended in EOF or a suppressed tail timeout. Exact response bytes cannot reconstruct a transport exception; the observation exists only on the transient adapter. The three-way contract is not preserved through this existing production durable boundary.
master_requirements: 8 CAUSAL PRECEDENCE: success primary plus timeout diagnostic
findings.reproduction: reviews/reviewer-2-repro-result.json: timeout owner is unclean; projected_provider_state_keys and persisted_attempt_tail_keys show no persisted tail representation.
findings.required_boundary: Carry and seal the owner outcome after response/transport close in the production execution ledger, separately from legacy transport_complete; verify reload preserves it. No automatic fix performed.
